content.text:
Dear Employee,

Following the incident on October 18, 2027, in which the counterbalance truck you were driving struck racking, I have made a decision on the allegation that you drove the truck when your forklift authorization had expired.

Outcome: You are receiving a first written warning. This decision was made on October 22, 2027.

Reasons for this decision:

You drove the counterbalance truck when your authorization had run out, and the fork hit an upright. You told me that no one warned you the authorization had expired, and the company register shows that no reminder was sent to anyone in 2027. You also reported that a pallet was in the aisle at the time.

I have taken these points into account: there was no reminder system in place, a pallet was left in the aisle, and you have six years of clean service with the company. However, driving without a current authorization is still a serious matter, so I have given you a first written warning. I am also booking you onto a refresher training course.

How to appeal:

If you disagree with this decision, you may appeal to an external HR adviser. You must submit your appeal within 5 days of receiving this letter.

Yours sincerely,

Rachel Okafor
HR Manager
Ashby & Lowe

Driving without a current authorization is still serious, so I am giving you a first written warning and booking your refresher training.

Ashby & Lowe
